A result carries enough identity to show which code, inputs and solver
produced it. This page lists what a run and its report record, for anyone who
reads a run record or changes what one holds, and what public documentation
may contain.

## What a run records {#public-provenance-contract}

A run or report binds, as they apply:

- the SCGSim distribution version and the measured identity of the runtime
  source (its modules and their content);
- the SCGSim Git revision when it is truthfully known, and the backend's
  revision;
- the identity of the geometry source and its topology;
- the solver and schema versions;
- the machine profile and the run receipt;
- the identities of the config, mesh, handoff, result and report files;
- the validation and failure state.

Read a returned run folder together with the source and model records of its
preparation. A distribution version alone does not identify the code bytes,
layout, settings or native result of a study; the runtime-source manifest and
its content digest identify the module bytes that ran.

AEDT computes its runtime source on each use: the import closure of every
module under `scgsim/aedt` and the two AEDT visualization loaders, recorded as
`scgsim.aedt.runtime-source.v30`. Preparation and execution record their
module bytes and digest separately. A result whose runtime source has an
earlier schema is refused; read it with the SCGSim commit that wrote it
([AEDT runtime source](../reference/specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#runtime-source)).

The Palace handoff and mesh manifest have a field `scgsim_sgb`. It holds the
name of the geometry builder that made the model, today
`scgsim.geometry.sgb`; the field's name is historical and asks for no import.
An older receipt keeps the module names it recorded; they are not rewritten
to today's paths.

## What public documentation may contain {#publication-boundary}

Public SCGSim documentation and fixtures contain no private names, paths,
dimensions, screenshots, meshes, configs, receipts, data or artifacts.
Removing identifying details does not by itself make material publishable.

Validation on private data may support a public aggregate statement only when
that statement has its own permission to publish and contains no private
identity or payload.
